summary: Point-scanning with visible lasers; a pinhole in front of PMT, HyD or GaAsP detectors rejects out-of-focus light. Fixed tissue, slides, cell culture, live imaging at shallow depth.
status: Experimental. Our own wording of the cited sources; a cause stays 'consistent with' until the alternatives are ruled out. Scope feature lines are unverified until a facility checks them; `seenInFiles` is what the lab's own files record.

stages.does: Visible laser lines (e.g. 405, 488, 552/561, 638 nm), one or more per channel; one-photon excitation along the whole cone of light, not only at the focus.
Sets each line's power (AOTF or attenuator %), per sequence or track; some systems raise it with depth.

symptoms.explanation: Scattering and absorption reduce both the excitation reaching the focus and the emission getting back through the pinhole; with one-photon excitation the light above the focus also bleaches as you go down. Power raised with depth compensates part of it.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: brightest 1 % by depth falling; Light path: no depth compensation recorded.
symptoms.alternatives: Fewer labelled cells deeper (biology), antibody penetration falling with depth in fixed tissue, or a refractive-index mismatch with the objective's immersion.

stages.does: Moves the focus across the field: zoom sets the pixel size, dwell time (scan speed) the light per pixel, line or frame averaging the noise.

symptoms.symptom: Small structures span only a pixel or two, or the field is much larger than needed.
symptoms.explanation: Zoom sets the pixel size: resolving a feature needs a pixel about half its size or smaller (Nyquist); larger pixels lose detail, much smaller ones cost time and bleaching for nothing.
symptoms.check: Light path: zoom and objective; Image: pixel size against the size of the objects in question.
symptoms.alternatives: Coarse is normal when the question is a count or presence, not a size or shape; ask what the images are for.

symptoms.symptom: Grainy objects and background at short dwell with no averaging.
symptoms.explanation: Few photons per pixel: shot noise dominates. A longer dwell or line/frame averaging collects more, at the cost of time and bleaching.
symptoms.check: Light path: dwell time and averaging; Acquired data: noise.snr, photons.objects.
symptoms.alternatives: Weak labelling, a detector gain set low, or a pinhole closed further than needed.

stages.does: Focuses the excitation and collects the emission; NA sets resolution and light collected, immersion must match the sample.
Fluoresces, scatters, and bleaches under the light — including above and below the plane being imaged.

symptoms.symptom: Signal falls over the frames, or planes imaged later in a stack are dimmer.
symptoms.explanation: Each scan bleaches the dye, and one-photon excitation bleaches the whole cone of light, so a stack or a time series loses signal as it goes; live samples can also be damaged by the light.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: brightest 1 % by frame (and by plane in acquisition order); Light path: laser %, dwell, averaging.
symptoms.alternatives: Cells leaving the field or the focus drifting (look at the images), or real biological change.

stages.does: Rejects light from outside the focal plane; its size, in Airy units (AU), trades sectioning against signal. 1 AU is the usual setting.

symptoms.symptom: Out-of-focus haze (pinhole open), or a dim, noisy image (pinhole closed).
symptoms.explanation: A larger pinhole passes more light but thickens the optical section; a smaller one sections more thinly but throws away in-focus light too. Channels with different pinholes have different section thicknesses.
symptoms.check: Light path: pinhole (AU, µm) per channel or track.
symptoms.alternatives: Haze from a thick, scattering sample or diffuse staining; dimness from weak labelling.

stages.does: Dichroics, emission filters or a spectral detector pick each channel's band; channels are scanned together (simultaneous) or one after the other (sequential).

symptoms.symptom: The same objects appear in two channels.
symptoms.explanation: A dye's emission reaches another channel's band (bleed-through), or one laser excites two dyes (crosstalk). Simultaneous scanning lets both happen; sequential scanning, one laser per sequence, removes crosstalk.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: the channels' shared structure; Light path: sequential or simultaneous, the lines on in each sequence, the emission bands.
symptoms.alternatives: The labels really are on the same objects (co-localisation), or autofluorescence in both bands.

symptoms.symptom: Many narrow channels named by wavelength instead of by dye.
symptoms.explanation: A lambda (spectral) acquisition records the emission in narrow bins; the dyes are separated afterwards by linear unmixing against reference spectra, which needs single-label references acquired the same way.
symptoms.check: Light path: modes include spectral; channel names are wavelengths.
symptoms.alternatives: None: it is a mode, not a fault — but analysis that expects one channel per dye needs the unmixed image.

stages.does: Turn photons into a signal: a PMT's gain is its voltage (HV), a HyD's or GaAsP's a %; offset shifts the dark level.

symptoms.symptom: The brightest objects are flat-topped at the top value.
symptoms.explanation: Detector gain (or laser power) set so the brightest pixels exceed the digitiser's range; their intensity is lost.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: clipped % against the bit depth; Light path: HV / gain per channel.
symptoms.alternatives: None for the clipped pixels themselves; a bright artefact (debris, a dead cell) can be the clipped object.

symptoms.symptom: A large share of pixels sits at exactly 0.
symptoms.explanation: An offset set low cuts the dark noise at zero, so the background is clipped and dim signal near it is lost; background subtraction then reads it wrong.
symptoms.check: Acquired data: zero % with the floor called 'background clipped at 0'.
symptoms.alternatives: A photon-counting detector mode, where zeros are pixels with no photon — then the offset is not the cause.

symptoms.symptom: Images of one set that should be comparable differ in brightness.
symptoms.explanation: Laser %, detector HV/gain, dwell, averaging or zoom changed between images; raw intensities are only comparable at the same settings.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: per channel laser %, HV/gain; scanner dwell, averaging, zoom — compared across the set's images.
symptoms.alternatives: Real differences between samples or conditions, depth, or bleaching.

stages.does: Turns the signal into numbers: bit depth sets the range; accumulation sums scans.

symptoms.symptom: Few distinct grey levels, or dim and bright objects that cannot both be measured.
symptoms.explanation: An 8-bit acquisition has 256 levels: a gain set for the bright objects leaves the dim ones a few levels above background. 12 or 16 bit keeps more of the range.
symptoms.check: Acquisition: bitDepth per channel; Acquired data: the histogram's spread.
symptoms.alternatives: A sample with a narrow real range, where 8 bit is enough.

stages.does: Repeats the scan over z, time and tiles: z-step, plane count, frame interval, tile overlap.

symptoms.symptom: Objects jump between planes, or the stack is far denser than needed.
symptoms.explanation: A z-step larger than about half the optical section undersamples in z; much smaller costs time and bleaching.
symptoms.check: Image: z-step against the objective's NA and the pinhole; the size of the objects in z.
symptoms.alternatives: Coarse z is normal for counting or 2D projections.
